takeaway: The saphenous nerve runs with the long saphenous vein on the medial leg, outside the popliteal fossa.

question.text: Which of the following structures is not found within the popliteal fossa?

lines.text: The popliteal fossa is the diamond-shaped space behind the knee.
Its main contents, from superficial to deep, are the tibial nerve, popliteal vein and popliteal artery.
Also in the fossa are the common peroneal nerve, the posterior cutaneous nerve of the thigh, and lymph nodes.
The small saphenous vein joins them, piercing the fascia to drain into the popliteal vein.
The saphenous nerve is different: it walks hand in hand with the long saphenous vein.
They run on the inner side of the leg, medial to the fossa, outside it.
So the structure not found in the popliteal fossa is the saphenous nerve.
